title: Backend-only restart must not trip the scheduler mode guard

root_cause.what: Stage 5ZZN's guard ran UNCONDITIONALLY, before anything decided whether a scheduler would be started at all
root_cause.symptom: restart --no-scheduler was refused with 'this start would register 45 legacy entry job(s)', about a start nobody had requested
root_cause.why_it_mattered: it was the ONLY route to a backend restart, and 5ZZN had just documented that as the way to pick up the new dashboard API route
root_cause.the_deeper_harm: a guard that fires where no start happens is not a stricter guard - it teaches an operator to work around it, and the workaround here was `restart --scheduler`: restarting a live scheduler to rebuild a read-only backend, the more dangerous of the two acts

reproduced.note: 5ZZN itself had landed correctly - the operator ran the restart and the scheduler is in track1-only-shadow with 0 legacy entry jobs

fix.shape: the guard now fires at each of the TWO places a scheduler is actually started, not once at the top

site_1.why: 5ZZN's property, kept - a guard that fired after the kill would leave the operator with no scheduler at all

site_2.path: the cold-start path in the else branch
site_2.why_easy_to_miss: that branch starts a scheduler in legacy/default mode - the call passes no Track 1 flag - and both `up` AND `restart --no-scheduler` reach it when there is no scheduler to leave alone
site_2.consequence: a backend-only restart on a machine with no scheduler running is still a real legacy start, and is still refused
site_2.cost: nothing has been stopped on that path, so checking there costs the operator nothing

fix.relaxation: none - the guard covers strictly the same set of real starts

stage_5zzl_route_now_served.what_that_actually_was: the cold import chain on a freshly started backend, not the endpoint - stated precisely rather than left as 'it timed out'
stage_5zzl_route_now_served.conclusion: the day-slice cache is doing its job

regression_asserted_twice.twice: AT THE GUARD - a spy on legacy_entry_start_blockers proving a backend-only restart never consults it
regression_asserted_twice.why: a message that stopped being printed for some unrelated reason would pass a text check and prove nothing

what_must_stay_refused_is_pinned: restart --no-scheduler when there is no scheduler to leave alone (the case the fix must not open)

restated.was: pinned the literal source line `if not track1_only:`
restated.why_stale: this stage rewrote it to `if args.restart_scheduler and not track1_only:`; a source pin goes stale the first time the code around it moves and goes red for a reason unrelated to what it is about
restated.now: behavioural - ask for the transitional mode, watch it be refused, assert nothing was touched

tests.5zzj_alarm: NOW PASSES, and for the right reason: the running scheduler is in track1-only-shadow and registers no legacy entry job. It was left red at the end of 5ZZN precisely so it would only go green when that became true.

unexplained.what: the backend started during verification (pid 28320) exited at 23:04:53 with nothing recorded
ruled_out_by_measurement: no traceback in ops_backend.err.log or .out.log near the time
no kill entry in monitor/logs/ops.log - nothing in ops killed it
start_backend detaches with CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP | DETACHED_PROCESS, the same flags as the scheduler, so it was not orphaned by the shell that started it
unexplained.action: restarted with the same command, pid 46600, dashboard up
unexplained.if_it_recurs: capture whether it coincides with the market-view route's cold parquet read, the only new work this backend does
